sections.title: Registration Deadlines
sections.intro: As of Aug 2, 2026 — first day of school is Aug 19 (last day May 28, 2027). 🔴 3 items need action NOW. ⚠ = date or rate not published — call to confirm. Every number is tap-to-call.

cards.title: GISD New Student Enrollment
cards.brief: 🔴 Due Aug 17 — enroll both boys or they can't start on day one.

meta.text: Due: Mon Aug 17, 2026 · first day of school Aug 19
Bring: proof of residency, birth certificates, immunization records, prior school records

cards.desc: New-student enrollment must be complete by Aug 17 for the boys to attend the first day — walk-in enrollment is closed the morning of the first day until 1 PM, so there's no showing up and sorting it out. Gather the documents once and do both kids together. Do this first: Harang's electives (Theatre, Choir) are chosen during schedule building, and late pickers get whatever sections are left.

cards.title: RankOne Athletic Forms + Physical
cards.brief: 🔴 Before Aug 19 — online forms + current physical required for Harang's Pre-Athletics.

meta.text: Due: before the first day of school (Aug 19)
Only Georgetown HS trainers can clear a student — don't leave it to week one

cards.desc: Harang can't participate in Benold Pre-Athletics until every RankOne form is submitted online and a current physical is on file. Only GHS trainers can clear a student, so a last-minute scramble risks him sitting out. Pre-Athletics is where the tennis path starts this year — see the Benold card for why that matters.

cards.title: Palace Performance Company Auditions
cards.brief: 🔴 August 2026 — exact date unpublished ⚠ — call 512-869-7469 this week.

meta.text: ⚠ Auditions held every August — exact 2026 date not published

cards.desc: The Palace's advanced track: a year-long company with auditions every August. The exact 2026 date isn't published anywhere — which is exactly why the call has to happen now, not after school starts. If PPC doesn't happen this year, regular fall Palace classes are the fallback, and full classes often free up waitlist spots in the final week (24 hours to claim by email).

cards.title: Benold Electives — Theatre & Choir
cards.brief: 🟠 Chosen at enrollment during schedule building — late means full sections.

meta.text: Due: during schedule building at enrollment
⚠ 6th-grade after-school theatre schedule unconfirmed (site is login-gated) — ask when enrolling

cards.desc: Theatre (led by Glen Meadows) and Choir are picked while building Harang's schedule at enrollment — not add-later options once sections fill. The program site sits behind a GISD login, so the enrollment appointment is the moment to ask everything: section availability, after-school schedule, and how 6th graders fit in.

cards.title: YMCA Y Afterschool at Ford — Register
cards.brief: 🟢 Open now, rolling — register in person to start sooner than next Monday.

meta.text: ⚠ Current rate not published — confirm when calling

cards.desc: Registration for 2026–27 is open and Ford is confirmed on the YMCA's Georgetown campus list. The online system defaults your start date to the following Monday — register in person if Hanung needs to start sooner. Full program details on the After-School Care card.

cards.title: Fall Rec Soccer — Registration Closed
cards.brief: ⚫ Closed ~Jul 5 — one call to GSA about a late add, otherwise spring (~January).

meta.text: Closed: registration ran mid-May–Jul 5 · spring opens ~January
⚠ Late add unconfirmed — worth one call

cards.desc: Fall recreational soccer registration closed around July 5 (Force FC's uniform deadline was June 30). The realistic play: one call to GSA asking about a late add — ⚠ unconfirmed they'll take one. If not, spring registration opens around January; put a reminder in the calendar now so this doesn't repeat.

cards.title: Benold Tennis Tryouts — Aug 2027
cards.brief: 🟠 Real tryouts start in 7th grade — this school year is the bridge.

meta.text: Tryouts: August 2027 (7th grade and up only)

cards.desc: Benold fields no 6th-grade tennis team — tryouts start in 7th grade. The bridge this year: Pre-Athletics runs a tennis skills rotation three days a week, and Georgetown Tennis Center lessons plus GTA Jr. Team Tennis (see Sports) add the match experience a tryout will demand. Benold has courts on campus, so the goal is concrete and close.

sections.title: Schools
sections.intro: Georgetown ISD. Ford Elementary is walking distance. Benold Middle is a short drive.

cards.title: Jo Ann Ford Elementary
cards.brief: Top 10% Texas elementary, walking distance from home. PK–5, 538 students.
cards.desc: Ranked 461st of 4,651 Texas elementary schools. Student-teacher ratio 15:1. Strong Gifted & Talented program (top 15% statewide). Principal is Meredith Gandy. Same street as our house — Hanung can walk or bike. Hanung starts 3rd grade here Aug 19 — enrollment must be done by Aug 17 (see Deadlines).

cards.title: Douglas Benold Middle School
cards.brief: Harang's middle school — 6th grade starts Aug 19. Grades 6–8, ~8 min drive.

meta.text: 1401 N Parmer Ranch Blvd, Georgetown, TX 78633

cards.desc: Harang starts 6th grade here Aug 19. Activities: Theatre, Choir, Band, Orchestra, Student Council, NJHS, UIL, athletics, cheer — Theatre and Choir are electives picked during schedule building, so choose them at enrollment. The tennis path is the thing to know: 6th graders take Pre-Athletics, not UIL teams. Tennis IS in its 3-day-a-week skills rotation (forehand, backhand, serving, alongside volleyball/basketball/soccer/track; the other 2 days are speed, agility and weights), but real tryouts start in 7th grade — tennis, volleyball, basketball, soccer (cross country, powerlifting and track have none). Benold has courts on campus. Outside lessons this year (see Sports) are the bridge that makes the Aug 2027 tryout viable.

cards.title: Georgetown High School
cards.brief: Future high school for both boys. ~12 min drive. Strong athletics and band.
cards.desc: Assigned high school for both boys eventually. Enrollment ~2,083, UIL Class 5A, 12,500-seat stadium. Strong football and band, and — relevant if Harang stays with theatre — GHS has won state titles in One Act Play.

sections.title: After-School Care
sections.intro: Options for both boys after school ends at ~3 PM. YMCA at Ford Elementary is the standout for Hanung.

cards.title: YMCA Y Afterschool at Ford Elementary
cards.brief: On-site at Ford. 2026–27 registration is OPEN now. No pickup needed until 6:30 PM.

meta.text: Cost: ⚠ 2026 rate not published (was ~$60–80/week) — confirm when calling

cards.desc: Runs inside the school building — no transportation needed. Homework help, physical activity, STEAM enrichment, snack. 2026–27 registration is open and Ford is confirmed on the YMCA's Georgetown campus list. One quirk: the online system defaults your start date to the following Monday — register in person at the Y if Hanung needs to start sooner. ⚠ Confirm this year's rate on the phone.

cards.title: Boys & Girls Club of Georgetown
cards.brief: Backup option, ~12 min. Mentoring, tutoring, sports. Both boys eligible.

meta.text: Hours: Mon–Fri 3–6:30 PM; early-out from 1 PM

cards.desc: Backup option if YMCA fills up. Good for Harang who's past elementary YMCA. Mentoring, tutoring, sports, summer camp. Transportation from some schools may be available.

cards.title: Middle School Clubs & Sports (Benold)
cards.brief: Harang's practical after-school path: school clubs, theater, soccer, band.
cards.desc: For Harang, the social on-ramp at a new school is participating in clubs: theater, robotics, band, art, chess, and athletics: track, cross-country, soccer. Sign up at the start of each semester.

sections.title: School Calendar & Camps
sections.intro: GISD 2026–27 dates and the camp registration windows that open months early. The fall soccer signup closed before we knew it existed — this section exists so that doesn't happen again.

cards.title: GISD 2026–27 Calendar at a Glance
cards.brief: School Aug 19 – May 28. Big gaps: Thanksgiving week, Dec 21–Jan 6, Spring Break Mar 15–19.

meta.text: First day: Wed Aug 19, 2026 · Last day: Fri May 28, 2027 (early release)
Student holidays: Sep 7 (Labor Day), Sep 21, Oct 12
Thanksgiving: Nov 23–27 · Winter break: Dec 21–Jan 6 (return Jan 7)
Spring break: Mar 15–19, 2027 · Early release: Dec 18 and May 28
⚠ GISD approved new school start times for 2026–27 — confirm Ford and Benold bell times at enrollment

cards.desc: The three stretches that need a childcare plan are Thanksgiving week, the two-and-a-half weeks from Dec 21 to Jan 6, and Spring Break in March. Note the single-day student holidays too (Sep 21 and Oct 12) — those are the good days to schedule dentist and doctor appointments instead of pulling the boys out of class. One thing to verify: the district approved new start times along with this calendar, so don't assume the bell schedule matches what you're used to.

cards.title: Summer Camps — Registration Opens in February
cards.brief: Palace theatre camps open in February and fill fast. Set a January reminder; don't repeat the soccer miss.

meta.text: Palace camps: registration opens February, spots fill fast
Camp days: Mon–Fri 9am–4pm · early drop-off 7:30am, late pickup 5:30/6:30pm for a fee
Palace: incoming grades 1–12 · musical theatre, dance, acting, improv
⚠ 2027 dates and prices not published yet — check in January

cards.desc: Georgetown Palace runs full-day camps June through August built around rehearsing and performing an actual show — the obvious summer answer for Harang, and the extended-hours option makes it work as real childcare. YMCA of Central Texas runs day camps as the general-purpose alternative for Hanung. The thing to internalize: February is the deadline that matters, not May. Put a reminder in the calendar for early January so you're deciding rather than scrambling.

cards.title: Winter & Spring Break Coverage
cards.brief: Dec 21–Jan 6 and Mar 15–19 are the two gaps that need a plan. Break camps open ~6 weeks ahead.

meta.text: Winter break: Dec 21, 2026 – Jan 6, 2027 · Spring break: Mar 15–19, 2027
⚠ Break-camp dates typically post ~6 weeks out — check Palace, kidsActing and the YMCA in early November and early February

cards.desc: Winter break is the hard one at over two weeks. Palace and kidsActing both run break camps, and the YMCA covers the rest; none of them publish dates far ahead, so the move is to check in early November and again in early February. Worth noting the boys will happily do nothing for two weeks — the question is whether the adults can.

sections.title: Sports & Activities
sections.intro: Ninja Warrior (both love it from Frisco) and soccer. Local options to keep the boys active.

cards.title: Ninja Nation Austin
cards.brief: Same brand from Frisco. ~30 min drive. Classes, open gym, camps.

meta.text: Format: Weekly classes, open gym, camps

cards.desc: Same brand the boys already love — programs and obstacles will feel familiar. World-class course, coached classes by age/level, open gym, and summer camps. Book a trial class soon after the move.

cards.title: Move Sport Ninja Academy
cards.brief: Former ANW competitor's gym. Pflugerville, ~30 min. Competition-track training.

meta.text: Coach: Andy Lowes (former American Ninja Warrior)

cards.desc: Smaller, more personal than Ninja Nation. Run by a former ANW competitor with 15+ years of gymnastics coaching. Strong fit if the boys want competition-track training.

cards.title: Georgetown Soccer Association (GSA)
cards.brief: ⚫ Fall 2026 registration CLOSED (~Jul 5). Call about a late add or target spring (~Jan).

meta.text: Ray Thomas Jr. Fields, 2101 Maple St, Georgetown

cards.desc: 450+ recreational players plus Select/Academy programs (Force FC). US Soccer curriculum, volunteer parent coaches, age-grouped teams. Heads up: fall 2026 registration ran mid-May to ~July 5 and is closed (Force FC's uniform deadline was June 30). ⚠ Unconfirmed whether they'll take a late add — worth one call. Otherwise spring registration opens around January; set a reminder.

cards.title: City of Georgetown Youth Soccer League
cards.brief: Cheaper city-run rec league. $60 resident. San Gabriel Park, Saturday games.

meta.text: San Gabriel Park, 425 E Morrow St

cards.desc: Lower-pressure alternative to GSA. City-run, Saturday games. Good first soccer experience or complement.

cards.title: Georgetown Tennis Center
cards.brief: City-run courts + junior lessons 10 min away. Pre-register — no drop-ins.

meta.text: All players must pre-register — may need to call to have an account created

cards.desc: The city's tennis center: private and group lessons, clinics, junior programs and tournaments. Everyone must pre-register — no walk-up drop-ins — and you may need to call first to get an account created. Coach Zach is a Georgetown High grad and former varsity player who reached USTA Champ Level as a junior (USPTR certified) — the right coach to aim Harang at next August's Benold tryouts.

cards.title: GTA — USTA Jr. Team Tennis
cards.brief: League match play, ages 4–18 — the closest thing to the school team he can't join yet.

meta.text: ⚠ Fall league start date not published — check the site

cards.desc: Georgetown Tennis Association's USTA Jr. Team Tennis combines tennis with team-sport structure — serving, rallying and scoring learned through actual match play. Since Benold has no 6th-grade team, this is the best substitute year: a team environment, real matches, USTA structure. ⚠ Fall league start date isn't published yet — check the site or ask at the Tennis Center.

cards.title: AcroTex Gymnastics — Ninja Classes
cards.brief: Combined gymnastics + ninja in Round Rock. ~25 min. Closer alternative.
cards.desc: Combined gymnastics + ninja classes. Backup option closer to home if Austin commute gets old.

cards.title: Sport Clips Family YMCA — Georgetown
cards.brief: Family membership covers basketball, swim, soccer, gym. ~12 min, ~$80–100/mo.
cards.desc: Basketball, soccer, swim lessons, summer day camps for kids — plus gym and fitness classes for parents. Single family membership covers many programs. Strong value.

sections.title: Theater, Acting & Music Lessons
sections.intro: Harang loves acting and singing. Hanung wants to play drums. Programs near Georgetown.

cards.title: Georgetown Palace Theatre — Education Dept.
cards.brief: Year-round acting, musical theater, voice, improv. Grades 1–12. Downtown, ~10 min.

meta.text: Doug Smith Performance Center, 206 W 2nd St, Georgetown, TX 78626
Programs: Acting, musical theater, voice, improv, dance, film & TV, stage combat
Format: After-school classes, weekend classes, seasonal camps

cards.desc: The hub for performing arts in Georgetown — established 2005, serving thousands of Central Texas students. Acting, voice, dance, improv, sketch, stage combat, even magic, ages 4–adult, and every session ends in a public performance. The advanced track is the Palace Performance Company: a year-long commitment with auditions every August — the 2026 date isn't published, so call now (see Deadlines). Pro tip: if a class shows full, join the waitlist — spots often open in the final week before registration closes, with 24 hours to claim by email.

cards.title: Benold Theatre & Choir
cards.brief: On-campus theatre elective + student activity, led by Glen Meadows. Free.

meta.text: Benold Middle School, 1401 N Parmer Ranch Blvd
⚠ Program site requires GISD login — details open up once enrolled

cards.desc: Theatre runs at Benold as both an elective and a student activity, led by Glen Meadows; Choir is separate and also available. Both are chosen during schedule building — lock them in at enrollment (see Deadlines). Free, on campus, and stacks fine with evening Palace classes.

cards.title: Arts Avenue — Georgetown
cards.brief: Theater + dance classes downtown. Multiple skill levels.

meta.text: 610 N Austin Ave, Suite 125, Georgetown, TX 78628

cards.desc: Theater classes alongside dance programs. Multiple skill levels. Alternative to the Palace Theatre for Harang's acting interest.

cards.title: kidsActing Studio
cards.brief: 16 Austin-area locations (including Round Rock, Cedar Park, Pflugerville). Pre-K through high school.

meta.text: 16 Austin metro locations (incl. Round Rock & Cedar Park)

cards.desc: Long-running theater program focusing on self-esteem, acting, and musical theater for Pre-K through high school. While their main studio is in Austin, they hold camps and classes at 16 local satellite locations. Convenient nearby options include Cedar Park (Live Oak Unitarian Church, Cedar Park Dance Co.), Round Rock (Grace Presbyterian, The Dance Spot, The Dance Gallery), and Pflugerville (Dance Elements) — all within a 15–20 minute drive from our house. Think of this as the backup if Palace scheduling conflicts — after-school classes, break camps, and staged productions, ages 3–19. ⚠ Georgetown-area fall semester dates unconfirmed — check the site.

cards.title: Austin Drum Lab — Georgetown
cards.brief: Kid-friendly drum studio in Georgetown. Decades of touring/teaching experience.
cards.desc: Run by Tony Miller who has decades of touring and teaching experience. Known for kid-friendly, patient teaching style. Right here in Georgetown — no Austin commute needed for drum lessons.

cards.title: Georgetown Music Sessions — Drums
cards.brief: Wesley Bennett — local drum teacher with years of glowing parent reviews. ~$30–45/lesson.

meta.text: Month-to-month, no contracts · in-person or Zoom

cards.desc: Wesley Bennett teaches drums month-to-month — no long contracts — in person or over Zoom, with years of consistently positive parent reviews. The sensible start for Hanung: sticks and a practice pad (~$25) for the first stretch before any drum kit enters the house. ⚠ Confirm the current rate when booking.

cards.title: Benold Band & Orchestra
cards.brief: Percussion continuation for Hanung once he reaches Benold (2029).

meta.text: Benold Middle School, 1401 N Parmer Ranch Blvd

cards.desc: When Hanung reaches Benold, Band is the school continuation of drums — the program keeps a Future Members page and a private-lessons directory. Nothing to do now except keep the private lessons going so he places well into percussion.

cards.title: Clark's Music Class — Georgetown
cards.brief: Private drums, guitar, piano. Patient, positive approach. Georgetown-based.
cards.desc: Private instruction with a patient, positive approach. Also offers guitar and piano if Hanung wants to try other instruments later. Serves Georgetown, Round Rock, Hutto area.

cards.title: Bach to Rock — Cedar Park
cards.brief: Private lessons + band rehearsals. Kids perform live. ~25 min.
cards.desc: Private drum lessons plus ensemble programs (Band/Glee Club). Kids get to perform live — great for building confidence. Fun, accessible approach for various ages and skill levels.

cards.title: School of Rock — Round Rock
cards.brief: Private lessons + weekly band rehearsals → live performances. ~20 min.
cards.desc: Private lesson plus weekly band rehearsal, building to real live concerts. At ~$300+/month it's a much bigger commitment than private lessons — the sensible sequence is a year with a private drum teacher first, then this if Hanung is hooked. Harang could join the same program on vocals, which would be genuinely fun.

sections.title: Gaming, Esports & Spooky Fun
sections.intro: Both boys love Fortnite. Harang is into Five Nights at Freddy's and horror. Places to play and compete.

cards.title: The Esports Cave — Cedar Park
cards.brief: ⚠ In transition — Austin location closed; Cedar Park running limited events while moving venues.

meta.text: Format: Open play, tournaments, birthday parties

cards.desc: Status check (Aug 2026): the Austin (Anderson Mill) location has closed, and the Cedar Park operation is in transition — running limited events while moving to a new venue in the Cedar Park area. Historically ran a monthly third-Saturday Fortnite tournament with prizes (~$6/hr open play) — that may return, but ⚠ verify on their events calendar before promising the boys anything. Players need their own Epic account for tournaments.

cards.title: XP League — Youth Esports
cards.brief: Structured youth esports league. Ages 7–17. Coached teams, regional tournaments.

meta.text: XPL Austin: 8127 Mesa Dr, Austin — ~35 min
Games: Fortnite, Rocket League, Super Smash Bros

cards.desc: Coached competitive leagues rather than open play — structured teams, an emphasis on growth and character development, regional and national tournaments. Like organized sports but for gaming. With the Esports Cave in flux, this is currently the most reliable competitive Fortnite outlet for both boys.

cards.title: YMCA eSports Programs
cards.brief: YMCA offers Gamers Night Out, eSports Academy. Strategy & sportsmanship focus.

meta.text: CHASCO Family YMCA / Twin Lakes YMCA
Programs: Intro classes, Gamers Night Out, eSports Academy

cards.desc: The YMCA offers structured eSports programs focused on strategy, communication, and sportsmanship. Lower-key than XP League. Check if included with our family membership.

cards.title: House of Torment — Austin
cards.brief: Austin's biggest haunted house. Professional sets & animatronics. Halloween season.
cards.desc: One of Austin's most well-known haunted attractions. Professional sets, animatronics, live actors. High intensity — perfect for Harang's FNAF/Little Nightmares vibe. Check age recommendations before taking Hanung.

cards.title: Scream Hollow — Smithville
cards.brief: Wicked Halloween Park — haunted hayrides, multiple attractions. ~1 hr drive.
cards.desc: Extensive Wicked Halloween Park experience with haunted hayrides and multiple themed attractions. Outdoor setting. Combine with a Hill Country drive. Great for Harang's horror interest.

cards.title: Fright Fest — Six Flags Fiesta Texas
cards.brief: October haunted-park season in San Antonio — kid zones clearly split from teen+ scare zones.

meta.text: Cost: park admission — check site for date pricing

cards.desc: The closest big 'horror, but actually fine for kids' event: Fiesta Texas splits Fright Fest into clearly kid-friendly daytime zones and teen+ scare zones after dark, so Harang gets the FNAF-adjacent thrill without the trauma. For the rest of spooky season: Scream Hollow (listed above) is the better all-ages haunted attraction, House of Torment is the intense one, and Alamo Drafthouse in Austin runs themed screenings year-round. Texas Renaissance Festival (see Events) is costumes and spectacle rather than horror.

cards.title: Escape Rooms — Austin / Round Rock
cards.brief: Horror-themed & family-friendly escape rooms. Multiple venues in the area.

meta.text: Options: Escapology (Round Rock, ~20 min), The Escape Game (Austin, ~40 min), 4 Dreams Escape (Austin)

cards.desc: Several escape rooms nearby: Escapology in Round Rock has family-friendly private rooms, The Escape Game in Austin has kid-friendly options, and 4 Dreams has creepier themes (zombie labs, abandoned attics) that Harang would love. Great for birthday parties.

sections.title: Gardening & Plant Shops
sections.intro: Harang loves gardening. Local nurseries and plant shops to buy flowers, learn about native plants, and get supplies.

cards.title: McIntire's Garden Center
cards.brief: Local staple since 1976. Native plants, trees, expert advice. Leander Rd.
cards.desc: Family-run Georgetown institution since 1976 — trees, shrubs, bedding plants, herbs, natives, perennials, cactus, roses and organic fertilizers, with a Certified Texas Nursery Professional on staff. Knowledgeable enough to teach Harang Texas gardening properly. Good natives to start the yard with: salvia, lantana, esperanza, Mexican feathergrass.

cards.title: Hillside Nursery — Williams Dr
cards.brief: Full-service garden center on Williams Dr. Plants, flowers, pottery. Closest nursery.
cards.desc: Right on Williams Drive — our closest nursery. Garden center plus landscape services, wide variety of plants, flowers, trees, and pottery. Perfect for quick weekend trips with Harang to grab flowers.

cards.title: Root to Rise Plant Co.
cards.brief: Boutique houseplant shop near Georgetown Square. Indoor plants, pots, repotting.
cards.desc: Cute boutique specializing in houseplants, pots, and plant accessories. They offer repotting services too. Fun for Harang to browse for indoor plants for his room. Near the Square so combine with a downtown walk.

cards.title: Hill Country Water Gardens & Nursery
cards.brief: Five-acre destination nursery with show ponds, streams and fountains — more botanical garden than store.

meta.text: 1407 N Bell Blvd, Cedar Park, TX 78613

cards.desc: Five acres of show ponds, disappearing streams, fountains, fish and garden art — worth wandering even when you're not buying anything. If the yard ever gets a pond or fountain, this is where it starts; they do consultation, design and installation too. Easy pairing with a Brushy Creek outing.

cards.title: Lady Bird Johnson Wildflower Center
cards.brief: 284 acres of native Texas plants in SW Austin. Peak season March–May. ~$12/$6.

meta.text: Cost: ~$12 adult / $6 child · family memberships available

cards.desc: The University of Texas's 284-acre botanic garden of native Texas plants — the definitive answer to 'what should we plant here'. Spring wildflower season (March–May) is the peak and worth the drive on its own; make it a half-day with lunch in Austin. A family membership pays off if Harang gets serious about natives.

sections.title: Georgetown — Parks & Daily Life
sections.intro: Everything within 15 minutes of home. More nature, water, and free family activities than you'd expect.

cards.title: Lake Georgetown & Trails
cards.brief: 1,300-acre reservoir. Goodwater Loop Trail, swimming, kayaking. ~10 min.

meta.text: Cost: Free entry; $5 parking some days

cards.desc: 1,300-acre reservoir surrounded by the Goodwater Loop Trail (26.6 miles total). Cedar Breaks Park has a boat ramp and swimming beach. Russell Park has campsites. Great Saturday outing — fishing, kayaking, hiking, picnicking.

cards.title: San Gabriel Park
cards.brief: 180-acre central park. Playgrounds, splash pad, river, BBQ. Free.
cards.desc: 180-acre central park with playgrounds, BBQ pits, splash pad, river access, and trails along the San Gabriel River. Hosts most city festivals and free events. Best free family destination in town.

cards.title: Garey Park
cards.brief: 525-acre nature park. Splash pad, dog park, river. $5 vehicle entry.
cards.desc: 525-acre nature park. Splash pad, dog park, equestrian trails, river access. Hosts Family Nature Fest in April. Often less crowded than San Gabriel Park.

cards.title: Blue Hole Park
cards.brief: Natural swimming spot downtown. Limestone bluffs. Free. Get there early.
cards.desc: Natural swimming spot on the South San Gabriel River in downtown. Beloved by locals on hot summer days. Limestone bluffs, shaded picnic area. Get there early on weekends — fills up fast.

cards.title: Inner Space Cavern
cards.brief: Underground cave tours. Walking + Wild Cave adventure. ~$15–25.
cards.desc: Underground cave system right off I-35. Multiple tour levels including "Wild Cave" adventure tours where kids can crawl through real passages. Memorable rainy-day option.

cards.title: Georgetown Public Library
cards.brief: Free kids programs, STEM workshops, summer reading. Library cards for everyone.
cards.desc: Modern library with free kids programs — Paws for People (kids read to therapy dogs), STEM workshops, summer reading program. Get library cards for everyone in the first month.

cards.title: Downtown Georgetown Square
cards.brief: One of Texas's prettiest squares. Free events most weekends. ~10 min.
cards.desc: One of the prettiest downtown squares in Texas. Free events almost every weekend: Pistons on the Square (3rd Saturday, classic cars), Second Saturday Market Days (Mar–Nov), Red Poppy Festival (late April), Christmas Stroll. Coffee shops, candy stores, indie boutiques.

sections.title: Day Trips (Under 1 Hour)
sections.intro: Half-day or full-day outings without overnight planning. Great Saturday options.

cards.title: Round Rock — Outlets & Old Settlers Park
cards.brief: Outlet mall + 645-acre park. ~20 min. Shopping + outdoor combo.
cards.desc: Round Rock has the outlet mall (great for kids' clothes/shoes) and Old Settlers Park (645 acres, baseball complex, fishing pond, playgrounds, disc golf).

cards.title: Cedar Park / Brushy Creek Lake Park
cards.brief: H-E-B Center (concerts, hockey), Lakeline Mall, splash pad. ~30 min.
cards.desc: Cedar Park has H-E-B Center (concerts, Texas Stars hockey, Austin Spurs basketball), Lakeline Mall, and the gourmet H-E-B. Brushy Creek Lake Park has fishing, paddle boards, and a great splash pad.

cards.title: Typhoon Texas — Pflugerville
cards.brief: Large water park. Slides, wave pool, lazy river. ~25 min. ~$45/person.
cards.desc: Closest large water park — slides, wave pool, lazy river. Buy season passes if going more than 2× per summer.

cards.title: Downtown Austin
cards.brief: Capitol, Lady Bird Lake, Zilker, Barton Springs, bats at sunset. ~40 min.
cards.desc: Texas State Capitol (free tours), Lady Bird Lake hike-and-bike trail, Zilker Park, Barton Springs swimming pool, the bats under Congress Bridge at sunset (March–October).

cards.title: Thinkery (Austin Children's Museum)
cards.brief: Hands-on STEM museum. Maker spaces, water tables. Free Wed 4–8 PM. ~40 min.
cards.desc: Hands-on STEM museum aimed at K–5. Maker spaces, water tables, light tables, outdoor garden. Excellent rainy-day Austin destination.

cards.title: McKinney Falls State Park
cards.brief: Two waterfalls, swimming holes, hiking. $6 adult, kids free. ~55 min.
cards.desc: Two waterfalls, swimming holes, hiking, biking, camping. Less crowded than Barton Springs. Best in spring and fall.

sections.title: Weekend Adventures (1–3 Hours)
sections.intro: Saturday-morning-departure trips. Hill Country starts ~1 hour west; Gulf Coast ~3.5 hours south.

cards.title: Fredericksburg & Hill Country
cards.brief: German town, peach orchards, Enchanted Rock, wineries. ~1h 30min west.
cards.desc: German heritage town, peach orchards (summer), wineries, Enchanted Rock State Park (huge granite dome — great climbing/hiking for kids), Luckenbach. Best March–May (wildflowers) and Oct–Nov (cooler).

cards.title: San Antonio — Riverwalk, SeaWorld, Six Flags
cards.brief: The Alamo, Riverwalk, SeaWorld, Six Flags, SA Zoo. ~1h 30min south.
cards.desc: The Alamo and Riverwalk are bucket-list. SeaWorld San Antonio and Six Flags Fiesta Texas are both there. San Antonio Zoo is one of the best in Texas. Easy overnight weekend.

cards.title: Waco — Magnolia, Zoo, Dr Pepper Museum
cards.brief: Magnolia Market, Cameron Park Zoo, Baylor campus. ~1h 30min north.
cards.desc: Magnolia Market at the Silos (Chip & Joanna Gaines), Dr Pepper Museum, Cameron Park Zoo, Baylor campus. Long day trip or overnight.

cards.title: Waco Lions Park & Kiddieland
cards.brief: Vintage 1965 kiddie amusement park — carousel, Ferris wheel, mini train, go-karts, putt-putt. Rides ~$2.

meta.text: Cost: no gate fee · rides $2 (6 for $10) · train $3 · putt-putt $5
Seasonal: roughly Mar–Oct, mostly Fri–Sun — check before driving up

cards.desc: Nonprofit amusement park run by the Waco Founder Lions Club since 1965 — carousel, Ferris wheel, mini train, go-karts and putt-putt at prices from another decade. Squarely Hanung's speed; Harang will still do go-karts and putt-putt. No admission fee, you pay per ride. Hours are seasonal and weekend-heavy, so verify on their page before making the drive.

cards.title: Waco Mammoth National Monument
cards.brief: Real ice-age mammoth fossils in a climate-controlled dig shelter. Grounds free, tours $5–6.

meta.text: Cost: grounds free · dig shelter tour $6 adult / $5 youth (4–17), under 4 free

cards.desc: National Park Service site built over the nation's only recorded nursery herd of Columbian mammoths — you see the real fossils exactly where they were found, from a walkway above the dig pit. Guided tours leave every 30 minutes, no reservation, and run about 45 minutes — the right length for kids. Ten minutes from Cameron Park and the zoo, so it stacks easily into a Waco day.

cards.title: Waco Surf
cards.brief: Surf lagoon, cable wakeboarding, lazy river and big slides. Water park from $14 (kids).

meta.text: Cost: water park from $14 kids · family pass $99 (2 adults + 2 kids) · surf sessions extra
Summer season (roughly May–mid Sep) · weekdays 12–6, weekends 11–7

cards.desc: The former BSR Cable Park, now a full surf resort: man-made wave lagoon with lessons, cable park for wakeboarding, lazy river, sandy beach and some genuinely big slides. The water-park side fits both boys; surfing or the new Shredmill standing wave is the splurge. Book online — summer weekends sell out — and there are on-site cabins if it turns into an overnight.

cards.title: Mayborn Museum Complex
cards.brief: Baylor's natural history museum with 17 hands-on discovery rooms. $8–10, best rainy-day option in Waco.

meta.text: 1300 S University Parks Dr, Waco, TX 76706

cards.desc: Baylor University's science and natural history museum — the draw for kids is two floors of themed discovery rooms where everything is meant to be touched. Solid dinosaur and geology exhibits, plus a walk-through historic village outside. The best indoor play in Waco when it's 100° or pouring, and it's five minutes from Magnolia Market.

cards.title: Cameron Park (Waco)
cards.brief: 416-acre river park: 20 miles of trails, 100-ft cliffs, Jacob's Ladder stair climb. Free.

meta.text: Along the Brazos River, Waco, TX 76708 — trailheads off University Parks Dr & Cameron Park Dr

cards.desc: One of the largest city parks in Texas, on 100-foot bluffs where the Bosque meets the Brazos. Twenty miles of ski-style color-graded trails (green to double black) that mountain bikers drive hours for, plus the 88-step Jacob's Ladder climb and clifftop river overlooks — very Ninja Warrior friendly. It wraps around Cameron Park Zoo, so the two combine into one stop. Bring water; the black trails are legitimately steep.

cards.title: Homestead Craft Village
cards.brief: Working craft village: blacksmith, pottery, woodworking, 1760 gristmill and heritage gardens. Free to visit.

meta.text: Cost: Free to visit · craft classes and food extra

cards.desc: An 18-acre working homestead village where craftspeople actually demonstrate blacksmithing, pottery, woodworking, cheese-making and fiber arts, centered on a restored 1760 gristmill. The herb and vegetable gardens are squarely Harang territory, and the deli/café does very good from-scratch food. Free to wander; the Homestead Fair over Thanksgiving weekend is the big annual event and worth planning around.

cards.title: Schlitterbahn New Braunfels
cards.brief: One of the world's largest water parks. Comal River runs through it. ~1h 15min.
cards.desc: One of the largest water parks in the world. The Comal River runs through it. Plan for a full day; arrive at opening. Season May–September.

cards.title: Gruene — Float the Guadalupe & Dance Hall
cards.brief: River tubing + oldest dance hall in Texas (1878). ~1h 15min south.
cards.desc: Tubing/floating on the Guadalupe or Comal River — peak Texas summer experience. Gruene Hall is the oldest continuously operating dance hall in Texas (1878). Easy combo with a Schlitterbahn weekend.

cards.title: Galveston & Gulf Coast
cards.brief: Closest beach. Pleasure Pier, Moody Gardens. ~3h 30min. Better as 2–3 night trip.
cards.desc: The closest beach. Pleasure Pier, Moody Gardens (pyramid aquarium + rainforest), Schlitterbahn Galveston. Better as a 2–3 night trip than a day trip.

cards.title: Dallas / Fort Worth
cards.brief: Previous home area. Stockyards, Perot Museum, DFW Airport. ~3 hours north.
cards.desc: Previous home and friends/family. DFW Airport for international travel. Fort Worth Stockyards (cattle drives, rodeo), Perot Museum, Klyde Warren Park.

cards.title: Houston — Space Center, Zoo, Museums
cards.brief: NASA Space Center, Houston Zoo, museums. ~2h 30min east. Plan 2-day weekend.
cards.desc: Space Center Houston (NASA), Houston Zoo, Museum of Natural Science, Children's Museum of Houston. Plan for a 2-day weekend to make it worth the drive.

cards.desc: Local institution since 1926. Famous "Texas-size" yellow donuts. Saturday morning kid bribery, sorted.

cards.title: Korean Grocery & BBQ — H Mart & North Austin
cards.brief: H Mart (Lakeline) grocery + food court, Charm K-BBQ. Massive selection. ~20–25 min.

cards.desc: Brand new arena on UT campus. Biggest touring acts play here.

sections.title: Medical & Dental
sections.intro: Who to call when someone is sick or hurt. Set up the routine ones before you need the urgent ones. ⚠ Confirm each office takes our insurance on the first call.

cards.title: Urgent Care vs ER — Start Here
cards.brief: Broken bones, stitches, fevers → urgent care. Head injury, trouble breathing, uncontrolled bleeding → ER, or 911.

meta.text: Urgent care: St. David's CareNow, 1205 S I-35 · ~12 min
ER: St. David's Georgetown Hospital, 2000 Scenic Dr · ~12 min · open 24/7

cards.desc: The rule that saves money and hours: urgent care handles sprains, cuts needing stitches, fevers, ear infections and the after-school injuries that look scary but aren't. Go straight to the ER (or call 911) for head injuries with confusion or vomiting, trouble breathing, bleeding that won't stop, or anything involving the neck or spine. Note the gap — CareNow closes at 8pm on weekdays and 5pm Sunday, so anything later is the ER by default. St. David's Georgetown is a Level IV Trauma Center and Certified Primary Stroke Center.

cards.title: Georgetown Pediatrics & Family Medicine
cards.brief: Accepting new patients, birth–18, 5 min away on Williams Dr. Call to establish care before someone gets sick.

meta.text: 4841 Williams Dr, Bldg C Ste 105, Georgetown, TX 78633

cards.desc: Confirmed accepting new pediatric patients, and it's the closest practice to the house — same stretch of Williams Dr as Hillside Nursery. Both boys can be seen here. They're part of the Austin Health Partners network, which opens up evening and weekend appointments beyond their own Mon–Fri hours. Establish care now: new-patient slots take weeks, and you don't want to be doing paperwork during a fever. ⚠ Confirm insurance on the first call.

cards.title: Georgetown Pediatric Dentistry & Orthodontics
cards.brief: Kids' dentist and orthodontist under one roof on Williams Dr — worth it with Harang at brace-consult age.
cards.desc: Treats infants through young adults and does orthodontics in the same practice — which matters right now, since 11 is when most kids get their first orthodontic evaluation. Handling both without a second referral office is the real convenience here. Weekday-only hours mean cleanings will cost school time; book the early slots and use the Oct 12 and Sep 21 student holidays if you can. ⚠ Confirm insurance.

sections.title: Korean Community & Language
sections.intro: Keeping Korean in the boys' lives — Saturday school, churches, and community in the Austin area. Everything here is a 35–50 min drive; H Mart is filed under Restaurants.

cards.title: Austin Korean School (한글학교)
cards.brief: Saturday Korean school since 1986 — language, history and culture, ages 4+. ~45 min south.

meta.text: Webb Middle School, 601 E St Johns Ave, Austin, TX 78752
⚠ Registration windows and tuition not reliably published — call or check the site before planning around it

cards.desc: A non-profit, non-religious Saturday school running since 1986, serving ~150 students with 24 teachers out of Webb Middle School. Beyond language it covers Korean history and culture through traditional dance, music and crafts — which lands better with kids than worksheets do. Be honest about the cost: it's a 45-minute drive each way and it eats the Saturday, so it only works if the whole family commits. ⚠ The registration dates floating around online look stale — confirm the current semester directly before counting on a spot.

cards.title: Korean Churches — Austin Area
cards.brief: Several established Korean congregations 35–50 min south, Protestant and Catholic.

meta.text: Austin Korean Presbyterian Church (AKPC) · The Lord's Church of Austin · The Blessing Church (Baptist) · 성 김대건 Korean Catholic Church

cards.desc: The Austin area has several long-established Korean congregations across denominations — AKPC and the Lord's Church of Austin are among the larger ones, with The Blessing Church on the Baptist side and 성 김대건 for Catholic families. Worth knowing even setting faith aside: Korean churches are usually where the community's practical network lives — childcare recommendations, tutoring, holiday events. The Austin Korean Association keeps a current list of congregations.

cards.title: Korean American Association of Austin
cards.brief: The community hub — events, Chuseok and Seollal gatherings, and a way in for a family new to the area.

meta.text: Austin-area Korean community organization · events and directory

cards.desc: The umbrella organization for the Austin Korean community — the practical value is the events calendar (Chuseok, Seollal, cultural festivals) and knowing who to ask when you want a Korean-speaking dentist, tutor, or barber. Georgetown is far enough north that the community won't find you; this is how you find it.

sections.title: 📰 Georgetown News
sections.intro: What's going on in Georgetown and within ~2 hours — refreshed every Monday. Week of Aug 7–16, 2026.

cards.title: Otaku Food & Anime Festival — Waco, Aug 15–16
cards.brief: Free two-day Asian food + anime festival. 100+ vendors, cosplay contest, sumo. Last weekend before school.

meta.text: Richland Mall, 6001 W Waco Dr, Waco, TX
Cost: Free admission + free parking · bring CASH for food stalls
100+ vendors · cosplay contest · sumo tournament · voice actors · photo ops

cards.desc: Free two-day anime and Asian food festival at Richland Mall — Filipino, Japanese and Thai street food, Taiwanese boba, baos, noodles, Vietnamese grilled chicken, plus 100+ food and merch vendors. This is squarely both boys' territory: anime, cosplay contests, a sumo tournament and voice actors, with food the family actually wants to eat. Bring cash — many stalls don't take cards. Timing is the selling point: it's the last free weekend before school starts Aug 19, and it stacks with the Waco cards below (Kiddieland, Mammoth, Cameron Park) into one full day. Sunday closes earlier at 5:30pm.

cards.title: First Friday on the Square — Tonight
cards.brief: Fri Aug 7, evening — live music, late shopping and food trucks around the courthouse square.

meta.text: First Friday of every month, evening

cards.desc: The monthly community night out: the square stays open late with live music, after-hours shopping and plenty of dinner options. Easy first outing of the school-shopping weekend — park once and walk. Repeats the first Friday of every month, so if this one's missed, September's is four weeks out.

cards.title: Summer Moon Coffee Opens Saturday
cards.brief: Sat Aug 8 — Georgetown's first Summer Moon, in Bluebonnet Plaza (1312 W University Ave).

meta.text: Bluebonnet Plaza, 1312 W University Ave, Ste 102

cards.desc: The Austin wood-fired coffee chain (famous for its sweet 'Moon Milk') opens its first Georgetown shop Saturday. Worth knowing beyond the coffee: Bluebonnet Plaza is the new Hwy 29 development that's also bringing Shake Shack and Velvet Taco to town — this corner is about to get busy.

cards.title: Water Tastes Like Chlorine? It's Maintenance
cards.brief: Aug 3–Sep 3 — annual system flush. Chlorine smell and brief discoloration are normal and safe.

meta.text: Runs: Aug 3 – Sep 3, 2026 (Round Rock, Leander, Cedar Park on the same schedule)

cards.desc: The city's annual water-system maintenance moved to August this year. Expect a stronger chlorine smell and occasionally a green or brown tint for brief periods — it's disinfectant conversion, not a problem, and the water stays safe to drink. A pitcher filter in the fridge covers the taste for the month.

cards.title: Kittens in the Library — Monday
cards.brief: Mon Aug 10, 11am–1pm — shelter kittens available to meet (and adopt) at the public library.

meta.text: Cost: Free (adoptions via Georgetown Animal Shelter)

cards.desc: The Georgetown Animal Shelter brings adoptable kittens to the library for two hours Monday. Zero-commitment cuteness, dangerous levels of 'can we keep one'. Last free-form fun Monday before school-prep week kicks in.

cards.title: '42nd Street' at the Palace — Through Aug 30
cards.brief: The big tap-dance musical on the Springer Stage — good scouting trip before Harang's Palace classes.
cards.desc: The classic backstage musical runs weekends through the end of August. Beyond a fun family show, it's a smart scouting trip: this is the stage and the company Harang would be working toward through Palace Education and PPC — let him see the ceiling before auditions.

cards.title: Backpack Bash Sat Aug 15 · School Starts Aug 19
cards.brief: Free BBQ + backpack giveaway Sat Aug 15, noon, 1003 S Austin Ave — then it's go time.

meta.text: Sat Aug 15, 12:00pm · first day of school Wed Aug 19

cards.desc: Community back-to-school BBQ and backpack giveaway Saturday at noon. Heads up: it collides with the Otaku festival in Waco the same day — Backpack Bash is a quick local stop, the festival is a half-day drive, so pick one or do the Bash at noon and skip Waco. It's also the unofficial deadline for our own countdown: enrollment must be done by Aug 17 and RankOne forms before the 19th — all tracked in the Deadlines tab up top.
